page: Hetzner Cloud cpx11 is an entry-level virtual server powered by the x86_64 architecture and AMD EPYC processors running at 2.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 shared vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and a thread-per-core ratio of 1.0. It features 2.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 0.98 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with 40 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. The virtualization is managed via the QEMU hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the shared CPU allocation and low memory capacity limit the instance to entry-level workloads. In stress-ng testing, both single-core (754.39) and multi-core (1524.77) CPU performance fall into the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds measured at 31.66 GB/sec and 18.69 GB/sec respectively, placing them in the bottom 25%. However, single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves an average rating at 9.86 GB/sec, and LLM text generation using a small 135M model reaches 120.03 tokens/sec, which is also in the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of the cpx11 instance is the shared CPU model, which introduces potential resource contention and results in lower overall processing throughput, as seen in the weak Passmark CPU score of 4396.25 and poor static web serving throughput of 2.4 GB/sec. Qualitatively, this server offers a highly cost-efficient entry point for non-critical, low-resource tasks due to its low hardware footprint. It is suitable for lightweight applications such as basic development environments, small-scale utility scripting, low-traffic web serving, and simple background workers that do not require sustained high-performance compute or memory resources.
